Add the tofu and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the edges are browned and the center is hot. Add the mushroom, cabbage, and ginger if using and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the mushrooms soften and the cabbage wilts. Stir in the soy sauce with carrot or green onion if using, toss for 1 minute until the tofu and vegetables are glossy, and serve over rice if using.

name: Honey Soy Chicken Pepper Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining. Add the bell pepper and onion if using and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes until the vegetables start to soften but still keep some bite. Stir in the soy sauce with honey and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the chicken and peppers are glossy and coated. Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Miso Shrimp Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the shrimp and cook with the miso for 1 to 2 minutes per side until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes. Add the broccoli and carrot if using and cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are crisp-tender. Stir in the green onion and any extra sauce from the pan, toss for 1 minute until the shrimp and vegetables are coated, and serve over rice if using.

name: Garlic Bok Choy Beef Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and sear the steak strips with garlic and soy sauce until the meat is browned and cooked through. Add the vegetables in stages so the firm ones soften first and the quick vegetables stay crisp-tender. Pour in the sauce ingredients and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until the stir-fry turns shiny and clings lightly to the steak and vegetables.

name: Sesame Edamame Tofu Stir-Fry
instructions:
Pat the tofu dry, cut it into cubes, and set the rice to cook first if using.
Cook the tofu in a hot skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil and sesame oil if using for 6 to 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned on several sides.
Add the edamame and carrot if using, then stir-fry for 2 minutes until the edamame is hot and the carrot starts to soften.
Pour in the soy sauce and the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, then toss for 1 minute until the tofu is coated and glossy.
Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Ginger Carrot Chicken Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the chicken and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring every minute, until the pieces are browned and no longer pink in the center; add the ginger and garlic if using during the last minute. Add the carrots and cabbage if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the carrots are tender-crisp and the cabbage is soft. Pour in the soy sauce and stir for 30 seconds until the sauce covers the chicken and vegetables. Spoon over rice and top with green onion if using.

name: Sweet Soy Salmon Broccoli Stir-Fry
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little oil.
Cook the salmon for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned and just cooked through, then move it to a plate.
Add the broccoli and carrot if using with a splash of water, cover for 1 minute, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until the broccoli is crisp-tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and the remaining pantry sauce ingredients, then return the salmon to the pan and toss gently for 1 minute until glossy and heated through.
Finish with green onion and serve over rice if using.

name: Sriracha Garlic Shrimp Cabbage Stir-Fry
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with a small splash of oil. Add the shrimp and cook for 1 minute per side until they start to turn pink. Add the cabbage and carrot if using and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the shrimp are fully opaque and curled into loose C-shapes and the cabbage starts to soften. Pour in the soy sauce, toss for 30 seconds until everything is lightly glazed, and serve over rice with green onion if using.

name: Salmon Edamame Fried Rice
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with sesame oil if using. Add the salmon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until the center is opaque and the fish flakes with a fork; add the ginger if using during the last minute. Break the salmon into bite-size pieces and move it to one side of the pan. Scramble the egg on the open side until just set, then add the rice, edamame, and carrot if using and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the rice is hot and a few grains are browned. Stir in the green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Chicken Scallion Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the chicken with soy sauce and garlic until the meat is browned and cooked through, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Garlic Sesame Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the tofu with garlic and sesame oil until the tofu is browned on the edges, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Pineapple Shrimp Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the shrimp with soy sauce and garlic until the shrimp turn pink and curl, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Beef Broccoli Fried Rice
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with sesame oil if using. Add the beef and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up as needed, until browned and cooked through; add the ginger if using during the last minute. Push the beef to one side, scramble the egg on the open side until just set, then add the rice, broccoli, and carrot if using. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the broccoli is crisp-tender and the rice is hot with a few browned edges. Stir in the green onion if using and serve hot.

name: Tofu Carrot Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the tofu with soy sauce and sesame oil until the tofu is browned on the edges, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Tuna Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the tuna with soy sauce and garlic until the tuna mixture is warmed through, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Pork Cabbage Fried Rice
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the pork with ginger for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and no pink remains.
Add the cabbage and any carrot, then cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Push the pork mixture to one side, add the egg, and scramble for 30 to 60 seconds until just set.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until hot and lightly browned in spots.
Fold in the green onion and sesame oil, if using, and serve.

name: Miso Mushroom Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the tofu with miso and sesame oil until the tofu is browned on the edges, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Chili Garlic Shrimp Fried Rice
instructions: Use cold rice if you have it so the grains stay separate in the pan. Cook the shrimp with garlic and chili sauce until the shrimp turn pink and curl, push it to the side, and scramble any egg until just set. Add the rice and vegetables, stir-fry over medium-high heat until the grains pick up color, then return everything to the center and season with soy sauce before serving.

name: Miso Glazed Salmon with Rice
instructions:
Roast the salmon and broccoli at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes, spreading the miso over the salmon if using and drizzling the broccoli with sesame oil if using, until the salmon reaches 145F or flakes easily and the broccoli has browned edges.
Toss the broccoli in the pan juices for 30 seconds, then set the salmon and broccoli over the rice.
Rest the pan for 1 minute, then scatter green onion if using over the bowls and serve.

name: Soy Ginger Baked Cod with Rice
instructions: Heat the oven to 425F and season the cod with soy sauce and ginger while the pan heats. Roast the protein and vegetables until the fish flakes easily and the edges of the vegetables are lightly caramelized, checking at the halfway mark so nothing overcooks. Serve the roasted protein with rice or the pan vegetables and spoon any hot juices from the tray over the top.

name: Teriyaki Sheet Pan Chicken and Broccoli
instructions: Heat the oven to 425F and season the chicken with teriyaki sauce and garlic while the pan heats. Roast the protein and vegetables until the meat is browned and cooked through and the edges of the vegetables are lightly caramelized, checking at the halfway mark so nothing overcooks. Serve the roasted protein with rice or the pan vegetables and spoon any hot juices from the tray over the top.

name: Sesame Ginger Salmon Sheet Pan
instructions:
Roast the salmon, green beans, and carrot if using at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes, drizzling the pan with soy sauce if using, until the salmon reaches 145F or flakes easily and the vegetables are tender-crisp with browned spots.
Toss the green beans and carrot in the pan juices for 30 seconds, then set the salmon and vegetables over the rice.
Rest the pan for 1 minute, then scatter green onion if using over the bowls and serve.

name: Honey Soy Tilapia with Rice
instructions: Heat the oven to 425F and season the tilapia with soy sauce and honey while the pan heats. Roast the protein and vegetables until the fish flakes easily and the edges of the vegetables are lightly caramelized, checking at the halfway mark so nothing overcooks. Serve the roasted protein with rice or the pan vegetables and spoon any hot juices from the tray over the top.

name: Miso Butter Shrimp Foil Packets
instructions:
Fold the shrimp, broccoli, carrot if using, and miso if using into a sealed foil packet set on a sheet pan, then roast at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes until the shrimp are pink, opaque, and curled and the broccoli is tender.
Rest the packet for 1 minute, then open it carefully to release the steam.
Toss the shrimp and vegetables in the packet juices for 30 seconds and serve over rice with green onion if using.

name: Ginger Garlic White Fish Plates
instructions:
Roast the white fish, bok choy, and carrot if using at 425F for 10 to 12 minutes, drizzling the fish with soy sauce if using, until the fish flakes easily and the bok choy stems are tender.
Toss the bok choy and carrot in the pan juices for 30 seconds, then set the fish and vegetables over the rice.
Rest the pan for 1 minute, then scatter green onion if using over the bowls and serve.

name: Sticky Soy Chicken Thigh Tray
instructions:
Roast the chicken thighs over the cabbage and carrot if using at 425F for 20 to 22 minutes, scattering the garlic over the vegetables if using, until the chicken reaches 165F and the cabbage has browned edges.
Scatter the green onion over the pan for the last 2 minutes if using, then rest the pan for 1 minute.
Toss the cabbage in the pan juices for 30 seconds and spoon the chicken and vegetables over rice.

name: Japanese-Inspired Chicken Curry Rice
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat and cook the potato with the onion and carrot, if using, for 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is softened.
Stir in the curry powder, add the chicken, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the pieces are opaque on the outside.
Add enough water to mostly cover the chicken and vegetables, bring to a gentle boil, then lower to medium-low heat.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the potato is fork-tender and the chicken reaches 165F.
Fold the mashed potato back into the broth to thicken the curry, then serve over hot rice.

name: Japanese-Inspired Beef Curry Bowls
instructions:
Heat a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion if using for 3 to 4 minutes until softened, then stir in the curry powder if using for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef, potato, carrot if using, and enough water to come just below the beef and vegetables, then bring the pot to a boil.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover partially, and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes until the beef is cooked through, the potatoes are fork-tender, and the broth is lightly thickened. Spoon the curry over hot rice and serve.

name: Thai-Inspired Coconut Shrimp Curry
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic over medium heat until softened, then stir in red curry paste and garlic for 30 seconds so the pan smells fragrant. Add the shrimp with the vegetables and simmer until the shrimp turn pink and curl and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Taste for salt or lime at the end and serve the curry over hot rice while the sauce is still silky.

name: Thai-Inspired Coconut Salmon Curry
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic over medium heat until softened, then stir in red curry paste and ginger for 30 seconds so the pan smells fragrant. Add the salmon with the vegetables and simmer until the fish flakes easily and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Taste for salt or lime at the end and serve the curry over hot rice while the sauce is still silky.

name: Thai-Inspired Tofu Green Bean Curry
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic over medium heat until softened, then stir in red curry paste and garlic for 30 seconds so the pan smells fragrant. Add the tofu with the vegetables and simmer until the tofu is browned on the edges and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Taste for salt or lime at the end and serve the curry over hot rice while the sauce is still silky.

name: Vietnamese-Inspired Caramel Chicken Bowls
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic over medium heat until softened, then stir in soy sauce and honey for 30 seconds so the pan smells fragrant. Add the chicken with the vegetables and simmer until the meat is browned and cooked through and the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon. Taste for salt or lime at the end and serve the curry over hot rice while the sauce is still silky.

name: Chipotle Shrimp Tacos
instructions:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side so they stay flexible.
Cook the shrimp over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side until they are pink, opaque, and curled into loose C-shapes.
Squeeze in the lime and toss in the cabbage if using for 30 seconds until lightly wilted.
Fill the tortillas with the shrimp and top with mayo and cilantro if using.

name: Garlic Lime Fish Tacos
instructions: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil so they stay flexible. Cook the white fish with garlic and lime until the fish flakes easily, then add any quick vegetables or sauce so the filling stays juicy but not watery. Pile the filling into the tortillas, finish with the cold toppings, and serve right away while the tortillas are still soft.

name: Adobo Chicken Tacos
instructions: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil so they stay flexible. Cook the chicken with tomato sauce and chili powder until the meat is browned and cooked through, then add any quick vegetables or sauce so the filling stays juicy but not watery. Pile the filling into the tortillas, finish with the cold toppings, and serve right away while the tortillas are still soft.

name: Chile Lime Beef Tacos
instructions: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil so they stay flexible. Cook the beef with lime and chili powder until the meat is browned and cooked through, then add any quick vegetables or sauce so the filling stays juicy but not watery. Pile the filling into the tortillas, finish with the cold toppings, and serve right away while the tortillas are still soft.

name: Crispy Potato Poblano Tacos
instructions: Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil so they stay flexible. Cook the potato with onion and chili powder until everything is hot and well seasoned, then add any quick vegetables or sauce so the filling stays juicy but not watery. Pile the filling into the tortillas, finish with the cold toppings, and serve right away while the tortillas are still soft.

name: Street Corn Chicken Tostadas
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F and prep the filling with lime and chili powder so it tastes seasoned before it goes into the pan. Cook the tuna with garlic and the pantry seasonings until it is fully cooked and tastes seasoned all the way through. Spoon the mixture over rice, add dollops of yogurt plus the fresh toppings, and serve while the tuna is still hot against the cool yogurt.

name: BBQ Shrimp Green Bean Sheet Pan
instructions: Heat the oven to 400F and season the shrimp before it goes into the pan. Roast until the protein is cooked through and the vegetables are tender and lightly browned around the edges, checking halfway so the tray stays balanced. Rest the pan briefly before serving so the juices settle back into the food.

name: BBQ Chicken Bean Chili
instructions: Cook the onion and aromatics until fragrant before adding the broth and main ingredients. Simmer until the chicken and vegetables are cooked through and the broth tastes seasoned from the first spoonful to the last. Taste for salt or acid at the end and serve the soup while it is still hot enough to steam.

name: BBQ Salmon Corn Skillet
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium heat and cook the salmon until it is browned and fully cooked. Add the remaining ingredients in stages so the vegetables soften without losing all their texture, then simmer for a minute until the sauce clings lightly. Serve straight from the skillet while it is still steaming.

name: Chicken Pesto Rice Skillet
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned in spots and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Stir in the rice and the amount of water called for on the package, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fold in the pesto and spinach if using and cook for 1 minute until the spinach wilts and the rice is evenly coated.
Finish with parmesan and parsley if using, then serve hot.
